source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey! I wanted to send over the vision for the website.

The goal is to build a national brand website for SMASH ROOM that can support multiple locations and future franchise growth.

Main Website:
<http://SMASHROOMUSA.com|SMASHROOMUSA.com>

I want the design to be clean, modern, mobile-friendly, and similar in simplicity to iSmashUSA. Black, purple, and white branding with large images, lots of spacing, and easy navigation.

Homepage Sections:

Hero Banner
Location Selector
Rage Rooms
Axe Throwing
Splatter Room
Corporate Events
Birthday Parties
Reviews
FAQ
Contact

The homepage should immediately show visitors what we offer and allow them to select their location.

Current Locations:

Fairfield, CA
San Francisco, CA
Seattle, WA

I want each location to have its own dedicated page while maintaining the same design and branding across all locations.

The website should be built so future locations can easily be added without redesigning the site.

Future examples:

Phoenix
Denver
Austin
Franchise Locations

The overall feel should be a national entertainment brand, not a local business website.

value_updates.content_goal: Immediately show visitors what SMASH ROOM offers

routing_warnings.description: The broad claim that the Smash Room website is done concerns completion of the master-site build and does not specifically establish completion of the required homepage content.
The complaint that both websites are identical is clarified by the next message as a failure to distinguish the master location-selection hub from a location site.

The location menu and outbound location-site behavior belong to the master location-selection hub; the activity-listing clause restates rather than clearly changes the target homepage-content Requirement.
The client reports that Seattle and master-site profiles were placed on the wrong websites, which is a domain-to-site assignment failure rather than a change to the requested homepage sections.
